name: INFORMAL
description: Industrial design and product-development capability for products moving toward engineering and manufacture.
overview: INFORMAL contributes industrial design and product-development perspective where design intent, usability and engineering execution need to remain aligned.
projectTypes: Consumer, connected and physical products that need design direction, user experience thinking or mechanical development alongside a path to production.
collaboration: Dick brings the commercialization, supplier and program lens; the partner’s work is considered where it supports the project’s product and execution requirements.

name: TRULY
description: Electronics and display capability relevant to connected and consumer hardware programs.
overview: TRULY provides a technology-capability profile for projects where electronics, sensing or display considerations are central to product decisions.
projectTypes: Connected devices, consumer electronics and other programs needing an informed view of electronics, sensors, MCU or display requirements.
collaboration: Dick considers technical and commercial fit with the wider program before introducing any technology capability into a recommendation.

name: HENSIM
description: Manufacturing capability spanning moulding, tooling and assembly considerations.
overview: HENSIM represents manufacturing capability relevant to tooling, moulding and assembly decisions during the transition into production.
projectTypes: Physical products requiring an assessment of tooling, injection moulding, assembly approach or production readiness.
collaboration: Dick evaluates manufacturing capability against product requirements, commercial terms, quality expectations and execution risk before making a project recommendation.

name: Hardware Meetup
description: Community and event connections for hardware founders, practitioners and industry conversations.
overview: Hardware Meetup provides a community context for founder conversations, networking and industry events around physical product development.
projectTypes: Founders and teams seeking informed hardware community connections alongside their own commercialization work.
collaboration: Dick may point teams toward relevant community conversations where they complement a project’s needs; project support remains independent and tailored to the program.
